summary: Iteration 5 — FIX VERIFICATION for LOW-priority React duplicate-key warning on BatchHeader hold_reasons/required_actions lists. Both changes verified end-to-end: (a) BatchHeader.jsx now keys list items with `${index}-${reason}`, (b) backend release_checks in /app/backend/batches.py resolves parameter names via db.parameters lookup and emits parameter-specific messages ('Missing result for pH', 'Missing result for COD', 'Missing result for Appearance'). Also verified [data-testid=required-actions] with two IDENTICAL 'Re-run all tests' lines after a QA Return-to-QC of KEY-1: both li elements render cleanly, 0 duplicate-key warnings. context_for_next_testing_agent: Duplicate-key bug is FIXED and confirmed with browser console capture. KEY-1 was flipped from ON_HOLD to RETURNED during this run (QA return with duplicate required actions). All 88 backend tests still green. No outstanding action items.
rca of the issue: Iteration 4 refactor swapped array-index keys for the reason string itself in BatchHeader.jsx, but backend release_checks emitted the identical string 'Missing result for a specified parameter' for every missing parameter (fallback path when parameter name lookup failed). Result: React saw N children with the same key. E1 fixed both the symptom (composite key `${index}-${reason}`) and the root cause (backend now looks up parameter names from db.parameters so each hold reason is unique per parameter). Verified: KEY-1's hold_reasons are 'Missing result for pH', 'Missing result for COD', 'Missing result for Appearance', 'No instrument has been confirmed for this batch' — all distinct, and even if they weren't (as in required_actions with two 'Re-run all tests'), the composite key prevents any React warning.
